problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+4y \\ 5x+10y\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$
worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}2\cdot k+4\cdot 3 \\ 5\cdot k+10\cdot 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2k+12 \\ 5k+30\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2k+12=0 \\ 5k+30=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to both of these equations is $k=-6.$
